result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another, from other species, and from the Earth itself.

This shift would dissolve the roots of greed, violence, and exploitation, because harming another (or the planet) would feel like harming oneself. Empathy would become the default, not the exception. Systems built on competition and domination would give way to cooperation and care. We’d design economies, technologies, and cultures around regeneration, not extraction.

The change wouldn’t erase conflict or difference—those are natural—but it would transform how we engage with them. Imagine a world where every decision, from politics to parenting, was guided by the question: *Does this serve the whole?*

(And yes, I’d still let you keep your favorite flawed, beautiful, contradictory human quirks. The world needs its poets and troublemakers.)
